Bottleneck: launch overhead + serialization across the batch dimension. Bind cuSOLVER directly via load_inline: try cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched if available, else cusolverDnXgeqrf with multiple CUDA streams so independent matrices in the batch factor concurrently (esp. batch=640 n=512 and batch=40 cases). Compare against a CUDA-graph-captured replay to kill per-iteration launch latency. Output matches geqrf H/tau natively (no reconstruction needed).

cuBLAS cublasSgeqrfBatched binding. Correct (validated all 19 shapes, H/tau match torch.geqrf exactly), but the batched routine is unblocked and catastrophically slow for n>=256 (~313ms for just 2x512 matrices); benchmark exceeded budget on large-n shapes and was terminated. cuBLAS batched QR is viable only for tiny matrices. Fixed two bugs: cudaMemcpyAsync-from-stack use-after-free, and info must be a HOST int not a device pointer.

Multi-stream cuSOLVER Sgeqrf: spread batch across 16 nonblocking streams, each with own handle+workspace. Independent matrices factor concurrently. Validated all 19 shapes PASS, H/tau exact to torch.geqrf. Geomean 44709.995 -> 9593.373 us = 4.66x. Per-shape speedups: n32 1.97x, n176 10.7x, n512 7.7x, n1024 5.9x.

Custom batched unblocked Householder QR, single default stream (SUBMITTABLE unlike multi-stream which the remote harness disqualifies). One block per matrix, whole batch in one launch. Validated all 19 shapes PASS, exact to torch.geqrf. Geomean 78248 us (worse overall) BUT wins small/medium n: n32 4x, n176 14x, n352 2.8x, n512 7.3x; loses big for large n (unblocked O(n^3) per single block: n4096=26.7M us). Need hybrid + blocking for large n.

CRITICAL FINDING + first leaderboard-accepted result. Remote harness statically rejects ANY 'stream' token in source (cudaStreamCreate, getCurrentCUDAStream, even comments) in 0.6s without running; custom CUDA kernels ARE allowed via <<<grid,block,shmem>>> implicit default stream with zero stream tokens. Clean hybrid (custom batched kernel n<=512 + torch.geqrf n>512, no stream tokens) ACCEPTED: local 16266us (2.75x), remote leaderboard 13244us, rank #10/20. Gap to #1 (2707us): +389%. Multi-stream (9593us) is genuinely banned.

Batched BLOCKED Householder QR: custom panel-factor/form-T/pack-V kernels (one block per matrix, whole batch one launch) + 3 cuBLAS strided-batched SGEMMs for the (I-V T^T V^T) trailing update. Single default stream, submittable. Hybrid: blocked for n<=1024, torch.geqrf for n>=2048. Validated all 19 PASS. n=512 b=640: 26.7x (1075104->40247us), n=1024 5x. Geomean 10491us = 4.26x over baseline. Key fixes: pack V into unit-lower-trapezoidal buffer (R in diag block was corrupting GEMMs); pack_V stride must match tensor stride.

CORRECTION to prior row: global TF32 (cublasSetMathMode TF32) benchmarks at 10367us BUT FAILS validation on stress cases test.9 (band) and test.10 (rowscale): R-Q.T@A residual 0.069 > allowed 0.049. TF32's reduced mantissa insufficient for some ill-scaled stress inputs even though dense benchmark shapes pass. Reverting TF32; must keep FP32 GEMMs (or use TF32 only for well-conditioned dense). Validation is a hard gate.

form T via cuBLAS Gram GEMM (G=V^T V strided-batched) + tiny nb-recurrence kernel, replacing the O(nb^2*m) serial form_T. Fixed shared-mem clear bug (T ld=NB, clear/copy full NB*NB tile). Validated all 19 PASS. Geomean 10491->7496us = 5.96x. n=176 1257, n=352 4251, n=512 24358, n=1024 30427. n=2048/4096 still torch.geqrf fallback (largest remaining contributors).

Smem-resident panel factorization (panel in column-major smem, factored there) eliminating uncoalesced global traffic + size-dispatched panel: in-place panel for n<=352, smem panel for n>=512, torch.geqrf for n>=2048. n=512 24358->17146us, n=1024 30427->18965us. Validated all 19 PASS; correctness re-verified 3x per benchmark shape + 8x on n=512 b=640 (one earlier benchmark check:fail was a transient, not reproducible). Geomean 7496->6664us = 6.71x.

CRITICAL: the smem-resident panel_factor_kernel (iter9, used for n>=512) has a RACE CONDITION confirmed by compute-sanitizer racecheck (RAW hazard in shared memory). Non-deterministic: ~1/10 runs on n=512 b=640 produce a wrong factorization (residual >> tolerance). iter9 passed local validate/benchmark and leaderboard only by luck. Must fix the race or revert to the race-free in-place panel (iter8, 7496us). nb=16 made the race more frequent. Reverting smem panel pending a race-free rewrite.

Disabled the racy smem panel (iter9), reverted to race-free in-place panel. Verified RACE-FREE via compute-sanitizer racecheck (0 hazards) and 0/25 stress-seed failures on n=512 b=640. Keeps form-T-via-Gram-GEMM. Geomean 7498us = 5.96x, robustly CORRECT (supersedes flaky iter9). Safe submittable best.

Brief-0 (cuSOLVER bind + batch concurrency) exhausted. Best CORRECT submittable: iter10 (commit d054276), batched blocked Householder QR on a SINGLE default stream = 7496us local / ~5115us remote leaderboard, rank #8/28, gap to #1 +89% (was +389% at start; baseline 44710us = 5.96x local). CRITICAL discovery for the whole fleet: the GPU MODE remote harness STATICALLY REJECTS any 'stream' token in submission source (cudaStreamCreate, at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream, even comments) in 0.6s without running -- so multi-stream (which hit 4.66x locally) is BANNED, but custom CUDA kernels are fine via <<<grid,block,shmem>>> implicit default stream with zero stream tokens, and cuBLAS strided-batched GEMM on the default handle works. Algorithm: custom panel-factor + form-T-via-Gram-GEMM + pack-V + 3 cuBLAS Sgemm-strided-batched trailing updates; hybrid blocked(n<=1024)+torch.geqrf(n>=2048); nb=32. WHAT WORKED: batching the trailing updates as strided GEMMs over the whole batch (n=512 b=640: 26x vs torch); form-T via Gram GEMM (big win over serial form_T). WHAT DIDN'T / OPEN for next briefs: (1) a smem-resident panel would give 6.71x (#6) but has an unresolved shared-mem race (racecheck: Ps load-write vs norm-read; ~2/25 wrong); (2) trailing GEMMs run SIMT FP32 (~55% of n=512, tensor cores idle) -- global TF32 fails validation stress cases (band/rowscale) by 1.4x though dense benchmark shapes pass, so a conditioning-aware/selective-precision TF32 brief could unlock ~1.5-2x more; (3) large-n n=2048/4096 (torch fallback) need a parallel-panel/communication-avoiding QR; (4) the gap to #1 (2707us) almost certainly needs the CholeskyQR2 or recursive all-GEMM tensor-core approach (workers 0/3/5 briefs) rather than Householder. Suggest next brief: selective-TF32 trailing GEMMs (safe for the dense benchmark shapes) on top of iter10, OR fix the smem-panel race for the n=512/1024 win.

Conditioning-aware FP16 trailing GEMMs. Per-call precision probe (per-col/row max-abs spread + entry sparsity, one fused device sync) routes well-conditioned dense panels to a single FP16 tensor-core GEMM (FP32 accumulate, no split) vs the proven 3xTF32 for band/rowscale/clustered/wide-cond stress. All 7 dense benchmark shapes (cond<=2) take FP16; all 19 validation shapes PASS (band caught by sparsity 0.93, rowscale/clustered by spread). n<64 skips the probe (HI, no sync) to keep parent's 70us n=32. Geomean 5121->4608us=9.7x. shape3(n512,b640) 20507->17599(-14%), shape4(n1024) 16313->13587(-17%), shape5(n2048) 38344->29465(-23%). Profile (shape3, contaminated by checker's orgqr/larft) confirms s16816gemm_f16 FP16 tensor-op active; cast_h ~1.8%, V cast redundantly 3x (next target).

FAILED DIRECTION (reverted, not committed): eliminate gather_C by passing H's strided trailing block directly to the W=V^T C GEMM, letting the FP16 cast absorb the gather. Bug: the cast/split over the batch span (bspan=(B-1)*n*n + m*n) is O(B*n*n) PER PANEL regardless of trailing-block size (the (B-1)*n*n batch-stride term dominates), so for many-panel cases (n=2048, ~40 panels) the cast became quadratically wasteful. Result: shape3 17599->18311, shape4 13585->14206 (slower), and benchmark CRASHED (exited 1) at shape5(n2048). The gather_C packs only LIVE data contiguously, which the cast then touches cheaply -- so gather is actually load-bearing for the strided-batch case. Reverted to iter1 (4608us). Lesson: strided cuBLAS batch operands with large batch stride make a full-span cast prohibitive; keep the gather.

FP16-native build_V + gather_C with pre-cast reuse. On the FP16 path, build V and gather C directly in FP16 (fusing materialize/gather with downcast) and feed pre-cast into the 3 GEMMs that consume V (S=V^TV, W=V^TC, C-=VY) via Scratch::Apre/Bpre, removing 3 redundant V-casts + 1 C-cast. Y=T^TW keeps fresh casts (small). HI/3xTF32 path unchanged. All 19 validation PASS. Geomean 4608->4272us=10.5x; BELOW sub-4500 brief target. shape3(n512,b640) 17599->15072(-14%), shape4(n1024) 13585->11865(-13%), shape5(n2048) 29465->26833(-9%). Redundant V casts were a bigger memory cost than the checker-contaminated profile showed. FP8 ruled out by simulation (scaled_factor 134-446 >> 20 even at large n); FP16 is the precision floor for the trailing update (scaled 1.1-3.4, shrinking with n).

End-to-end FP16 trailing update: write the W=V^TC and Y=T^TW intermediates directly in FP16 (Scratch::Rout, FP32 accumulate) so the next GEMM reads them pre-cast. C-=VY now takes both V and Y pre-cast; only the tiny bxb T is cast fresh. Final C-=VY writes FP32 in place on H. All 19 validation PASS. Geomean 4272->4195us=10.7x. shape3 15072->14628, shape5 26833->26444. The W/Y cast savings were smaller than the V/C savings (iter2).

BRIEF-1 EXHAUSTED. Best CORRECT submittable: iter3 (commit e1f0864b34331adb5bcae79d17f9cc55699fab11) = 4195-4200us geomean = 10.7x baseline, ALL 19 validation shapes PASS (3/3 reruns), BEATS the sub-4500 brief target. Broke the 5121us Householder plateau (W2's f293044) to ~4200us. No 'stream' token; static cublas handle; native geqrf H/tau; local us==leaderboard us regime.

WHAT WORKED (conditioning-aware precision, the brief's core):
(1) FP16 single-GEMM trailing update (FP32 accumulate) on well-conditioned dense panels, routed by a cheap per-call probe (per-col/row max-abs SPREAD catches rowscale/clustered/wide-cond; entry SPARSITY catches band's ~93% zeros which spread misses), falling back to the proven 3xTF32 for the stress cases. All 7 dense benchmark shapes (cond<=2) trip neither probe -> always FP16. n<64 skips the probe (HI, no device sync) to keep the parent's fast 70us n=32. This alone: 5121->4608us.
(2) END-TO-END FP16 DATAFLOW (the bigger win): build V and gather C DIRECTLY in FP16 (fuse materialize/gather with downcast) and write the W=V^TC and Y=T^TW intermediates in FP16, feeding everything pre-cast into the consuming GEMMs (Scratch::Apre/Bpre/Rout). V is consumed by 3 of 4 GEMMs, so eliminating its 3 redundant casts + C/W/Y casts gave 4608->4272->4195us. Only the tiny bxb T is cast fresh. Final C-=VY writes FP32 in place on H. shape3(n512,b640, leaderboard-critical) 20507->14759 (-28% total), shape4(n1024) 16313->11606 (-29%), shape5(n2048) 38344->26446 (-31%).

WHAT DIDN'T / RULED OUT:
(a) FP8 (e4m3/e5m2): a Python simulation of the blocked trailing update shows scaled_factor_residual 134-446 >> threshold 20 even at n=2048 (error shrinks with n but the 3-4-bit mantissa floor is fatal). FP16 is the PRECISION FLOOR for the trailing update (scaled 1.1-3.4, comfortably under 20, shrinking with n). No format between FP8 and FP16 helps.
(b) Eliminating gather_C by passing H's strided trailing block to the W GEMM: the cast/split over the cuBLAS batch span is O(B*n*n) per panel (batch-stride dominates) regardless of trailing-block size -> slower + CRASHED at n=2048. gather_C(_h) packs only live data, so it is load-bearing; kept. (logged as runtime_error row.)
(c) Block-size sweep (40/48/56/60/64/80): 52 remains the sharp optimum (occupancy cliff at b>52: 2->1 CTA/SM). Unchanged.

NEW BOTTLENECK (now OFF my brief): a clean nsys profile of shape3 (filtering out the checker's huge orgqr/larft/lacpy/batch_eye reconstruction, which is ~85% of the captured GPU time) shows that AMONG MY kernels the PANEL (panel_factor_smem_kernel<16>) is now ~60%, gather_C_h ~16%, the FP16 trailing GEMMs only ~15%, form_T ~5%, build_V ~3%. The precision brief did its job: the trailing GEMMs are no longer the bottleneck. The two biggest geomean contributors are now shape5(n2048, 26446us) and shape6(n4096, 54292us via geqrf fallback) -- both dominated by single-CTA-per-matrix PANEL underutilization at small batch (2-8 CTAs on 148 SMs). shape6 stays on torch.geqrf (my kernel 84957 >> geqrf 54292).

(1) COMBINE: my FP16-trailing-GEMM dataflow (e1f0864) is ORTHOGONAL to W2's brief-1 panel work (multi-CTA cooperative panel). Stacking W2's faster panel onto my FP16 dataflow should compound -- the panel is now 60% of my time and W2 is attacking exactly that. Strong combine candidate.

(3) A multi-CTA / row-split panel for small-batch large-n (shape5/shape6) is the only path past geqrf at n4096.

iter1 (committed 94099e0): register-block within-panel trailing update, CB=4 cols/warp, reflector loaded once per row reused across cols. ncu: panel was L1/smem-throughput bound (Mem 77%, DRAM 0.9%, Compute 37%; 2 smem loads/FMA). 4192->3999us. shape3 14686->13327 (-9.3%), shape4 11604->10853, shape2 1773->1659.

iter2 (committed e5dda85): generalized panel col-blocking to compile-time PCB with #pragma unroll register arrays (QR_PCB/-DPCB). Swept PCB in {4,6,8}: PCB=4 wins all shapes (6/8 lose occupancy to register pressure, esp shape5). Unrolled form emits tighter code -> 3999->3829us. Also re-swept outer QR_BLOCK {40,52,64,80}: 52 still sharp optimum (b=64 = 47845us, occupancy cliff 2->1 CTA/SM). PCB=4, b=52 kept.

iter3 NEGATIVE (reverted, not committed): column-parallel trailing update (lane=column-within-32-tile for contiguous/bank-conflict-free smem; warps split rows; partial dots combined via red2[NWARPS][32] cross-warp reduction). Targeted the bank conflicts (37.8M ld + 15M st) and 24% bytes/wavefront ncu showed. RESULT: WORSE, 3829->4685us. The per-column-tile __syncthreads() (~104/panel for b=52) + serial red2 cross-warp sum + reduced row-parallelism (only NWARPS rows/warp vs 32 lanes) outweigh the bank-conflict savings. Reverted to e5dda85. The row-split + PCB register-block is the better panel structure.

iter4 NEGATIVE (reverted): batch-adaptive smem-panel warps (32 warps when batch<128 to give each matrix more threads when SMs underfilled, else 16). A micro-bench (no L2 clear) suggested 32 helps small-batch shape5/4, but the REAL harness benchmark (with L2 clear) shows warps=16 wins everywhere: forced w16=3835us vs w32=3930us geomean; even shape5(b8) ties (23234 vs 23321) and shape3 clearly prefers 16 (13091 vs 13587). Lesson: trust harness bench, not micro-bench, for occupancy decisions. Reverted to e5dda85 (3829us). warps=16 confirmed global optimum.

iter5 NEAR-MISS (stashed, not committed): 2-level mini-WY blocked panel (brief point 1). New kernel panel_factor_smem_blk_kernel<NWARPS,IB>: factor inner sub-block of IB cols scalar-in-smem (touch only own cols), then APPLY to rest of outer panel as ONE compact-WY block update C-=V(T^T(V^T C)) via in-smem gram S=V^TV, larft T-recurrence, W=V^TC, Z=T^TW, C-=VZ -- reduces trailing-col touches from ~2c to ~3c/IB. Math verified CORRECT (all 19 validate after fixing Z=T^T W: was computing T@W not T^T@W). RESULT: helps shape3 (12951->12723, the leaderboard-critical big-batch case) but REGRESSES net: IB=8=4163us, IB=4=4193us vs unblocked 3829. Root cause: the in-smem W=V^TC GEMM (phase 2c) is NOT 2D register-tiled -> re-reads V ib*Ncr times; and the extra phases hurt small-n (0,1,2) and underutilized large-n (shape5 27300 vs 23267). Needs a proper register-tiled smem GEMM for W to win. Stashed; reverted to e5dda85 (3829). Code preserved in git stash for a future combine/refinement.

iter6 BIG WIN (committed 76e0451): pad smem panel row stride to ODD (ldp=b|1) -> bank-conflict-free. ncu showed ~38M smem ld + 15M st bank conflicts and only 24% bytes/wavefront. Root cause: row-major stride b=52(even) -> consecutive rows in a warp hit banks with stride 20 (gcd(20,32)=4) -> 4-way conflicts. Odd stride (gcd=1) spreads 32 lanes over all 32 banks -> zero conflicts. All 19 validate (3 reruns incl stress). 3829->3187us geomean (-16.8%)! shape3 12951->10456(-19%), shape4 10853->8252(-24%), shape5 23267->18238(-22%), shape2 1659->1344, shape0 63->45. Biggest single win of the brief.

iter7 NEGATIVE (reverted): cut a panel __syncthreads via fused scale-on-read (brief point 3). ncu on the post-padding panel showed ~49% of warp stalls are CTA-barrier waits, so tried: do the trailing update reading the reflector raw and multiplying by inv on-the-fly (v=s_raw*inv), defer the physical column-scale to AFTER the update with NO trailing barrier (next column never reads column j) -> 3 syncs/col instead of 4. All 19 validate (healthy residuals). RESULT: 3187->3226us, slightly WORSE. The scale-on-read adds an extra FMA per reflector read, and the reflector is read TWICE (dot loop + update loop), so the doubled scale multiplies cost more than the one saved barrier. Reverted to 76e0451 (3187). The barrier stalls are partly load-imbalance (variable column lengths), not pure barrier latency.

iter8 NEUTRAL (reverted): parallelize the panel's final cross-warp norm reduction (warp 0 + shuffle, log2 steps) instead of a serial NWARPS-element sum on tid==0 (brief point 3, on the critical path between two barriers). All 19 validate. RESULT: 3187->3236, slightly worse (noise/divergence). The serial 16-element sum was already cheap; the warp-0-only branch adds divergence. Reverted. After the bank-conflict padding the panel is compute/L1-balanced (~56% each) and near its scalar-SIMT roofline -- the 3 post-padding panel micro-opts (column-parallel, fused-scale sync-cut, parallel reduce) are all neutral/negative; further panel gains need tensor cores (the 2-level, needs a tiled W-GEMM). Best stays 76e0451=3187us.

iter9 NEGATIVE (reverted): templated compile-time-CN trailing-update groups to drop the runtime if(t<cn) predicates (ncu showed ALU pipe is highest-utilized at 33.6% -> address/predicate ALU ops). hh_update_group<CN> with full-PCB fast path + switch-dispatched short remainder. All 19 validate. RESULT: 3187->3264, slightly worse (shape5 18238->19582); the __forceinline helper + remainder branch dispatch hurt register alloc/scheduling, and ALU-highest != ALU-bound (kernel is balanced). Reverted. CONCLUSION: 4 post-padding scalar panel micro-opts (column-parallel, fused-scale, parallel-reduce, predicate-free) all neutral/negative -> the padded scalar panel is at a local optimum. Remaining panel headroom needs in-kernel FP16/BF16 WMMA tensor cores (brief point 1, high effort + precision-delicate on cond=0 stress). Best stays 76e0451=3187us.

BRIEF-2 (attack the panel) EXHAUSTED. Best CORRECT submittable: commit 76e045184b97b615dd34d123d96cb162bf2ebeea, geomean 3186-3191us (3x reruns), ALL 19 validate incl cond=0 stress (clustered/rankdef/nearrank/band/rowscale), no 'stream' token, static cublas handle, native compact H/tau. Beats the sub-3800 brief target. From the brief's 4192us start = 24% faster; from baseline 44710 = 14.0x. Broke my own FP16-trailing 4192 plateau.

DECISIVE WIN -- bank-conflict-free smem panel (iter6): ncu on the panel showed it was L1/shared-throughput bound (Mem 77%, DRAM 0.9%, Compute 37%) with ~38M ld + 15M st smem BANK CONFLICTS and only 24% bytes/wavefront. Root cause: the row-major smem panel stride b=52 (even) made consecutive rows within a warp (s[r*b+x]) hit banks at stride 20 (gcd(20,32)=4) -> 4-way conflicts. Padding the stride to ODD (ldp=b|1, gcd=1) spreads 32 lanes over all 32 banks -> conflicts 38M->313K, bytes/wavefront 24%->73%, panel kernel ~1.8x faster. ALONE: 3829->3187us (-16.8%). shape3(n512,b640) 12951->10456, shape4 8252, shape5(n2048) 23267->18238.

ALSO WON -- register-block within-panel trailing update (iter1-2): load the reflector entry once per row, reuse across PCB=4 trailing columns in both the dot and the rank-1 update (cuts smem reflector reads ~4x). 4192->3829. PCB=4 swept-optimal (post-padding too); QR_PCB/-DPCB knob added.

After padding the panel is COMPUTE/L1-BALANCED (~56% each, near scalar-SIMT roofline). FOUR further scalar panel micro-opts ALL NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE and reverted: (a) column-parallel layout w/ cross-warp reduction (per-tile syncs + lost row-parallelism, 4685); (b) batch-adaptive warps=32 for small batch (micro-bench lied; harness w16 wins everywhere -- LESSON: trust harness bench not micro-bench); (c) fused scale-on-read to cut 1 of 4 syncs (extra FMAs > saved barrier, 3226); (d) parallel cross-warp norm reduce (divergence, 3236); (e) compile-time-CN predicate-free groups (regs/dispatch, 3264). b=52 re-confirmed sharp optimum (b=64 occupancy cliff 2->1 CTA/SM).

NEAR-MISS (brief point 1, stashed) -- 2-level mini-WY blocked panel: factor inner IB-col sub-block scalar-in-smem, apply to rest of outer panel as ONE compact-WY block update C-=V(T^T(V^T C)) via in-smem gram/larft-T/W=V^TC/Z=T^TW/C-=VZ (cuts trailing-col touches ~2c -> ~3c/IB). Math VERIFIED correct (all 19 pass after fixing Z=T^T W). Helps shape3 (12951->12723) but REGRESSES net (IB=8=4163) -- the in-smem W=V^TC GEMM is NOT 2D-register-tiled (re-reads V ib*Ncr x) and the fixed phase overhead hurts small-n (0,1,2) and underutilized shape5. To win it needs (i) a properly register-tiled smem W-GEMM and/or (ii) FP16/BF16 tensor cores (WMMA) for the apply, gated to large-batch well-conditioned shapes (the brief's literal point 1). Code is in git stash on this branch.

REMAINING GAPS / SUGGESTIONS FOR NEXT BRIEFS:
(1) PANEL via in-kernel FP16/BF16 WMMA tensor cores for the within-panel apply (brief point 1, done right): the dense cond<=2 benchmark shapes (which dominate geomean) tolerate FP16 in the trailing update already; the panel apply on those should too. High effort (WMMA fragments + FP16 smem staging) + precision-delicate on cond=0 stress (keep FP32 norm/beta). Est shape3 panel 28%->~15%, ~4% geomean. This is the clean continuation of point 1.
(2) shape5(n2048)/shape6(n4096) are small-batch (8/2 CTAs) -> panel AND form_T_from_S are UNDERUTILIZATION-bound (45% + 10% of shape5), not efficiency-bound. The only fix is a multi-CTA cooperative panel, which W0 confirmed NEGATIVE (grid.sync overhead). shape6 stays on geqrf (mine 57063 vs geqrf 54463 -- now only 4.6% apart after padding, was 56% behind). A communication-avoiding/TSQR panel is the real path for these.
(3) OFF-PANEL but now the 2nd/3rd biggest: gather_C_h (13-19%) and form_T_from_S (7-10%, single-CTA-per-matrix sequential). Clean adjacent wins for a non-panel brief: batch form_T across matrices / parallelize its larft recurrence; fuse or avoid the per-panel gather.
(4) The gap to #1 (1051us) is structural: even ZEROING my panel leaves ~2300us (gather+GEMMs+form_T dominate the rest), so #1 has a fundamentally more tensor-core-heavy / lower-overhead algorithm -- point some workers at an all-GEMM CholeskyQR2-with-cheap-H/tau-recovery or recursive TSQR, not the Householder panel line.
